title: Send us bright one, light one, Horhorn, quickening and wombfruit.
html_source:
A sentence that begins like an ancient invocation or prayer ends with two references to childbirth. Throughout this chapter, the language Joyce uses evolves, from Anglo-Saxon and its Greco-Latin influences to Modern English. This parallels the theme of development and birth that is seen in the birth of the Purefoy child. Joyce manages to allude to both of these developmental elements in the chapter in one of his opening statements.

PROPOSED SUGGESTION: an invocation to the sungod Helios (“bright one, light one”)

Horhorn refers to Sir Andrew Horne, who in 1904 was administrator of the Holles Street hospital. Joyce plays a joke here at the expense of Horne, making his already phalic name a symbol of fertility.
